paragraphs: The company sells election technology, and states its aim as delivering systems that are transparent, secure, accessible and reliable. Its site says the business was formed through the acquisition of Dominion Voting Systems and now trades as Liberty Vote. It describes itself as an American-owned nonpartisan election technology company.

The product range covers the election from ballot design through vote capture to results reporting. An election management system runs the whole election project from one database. Ballot marking devices come in configurations for in-person, accessible and early voting. Central count scanners handle absentee, vote-by-mail and precinct ballots. An audit record lets officials review ballot images alongside how the tabulator read each ballot. The systems work with verifiable paper ballots.

Customers are the jurisdictions it serves, and the company says older systems were retired so each one runs supported technology. In late 2025 it submitted a voting system called Frontier 1.0 to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission for certification under VVSG 2.0 standards. The company is owned by its founder and chairman, Scott Leiendecker.

quote.text: Liberty Vote Corporation is a new, 100% American-owned nonpartisan election technology company formed through the acquisition of Dominion Voting Systems.
